articles.title: Photos: Avalanche floods kill eight, hundreds missing in Nepal’s Himalayas
articles.summary: Flash floods devastate Nepal’s Himalayas, washing away villages and infrastructure along the Bhotekoshi river.
articles.body:
Hundreds of people are missing and at least eight have been killed after an avalanche of ice and rock triggered massive flash floods in Nepal’s Himalayan region, washing away villages and infrastructure along the Bhotekoshi river.

Officials said 384 tourists, including 291 foreigners from India, Malaysia, the United Kingdom and the United States, were unaccounted for after Wednesday’s disaster, which struck at about 9am (03:15 GMT). Roads and hydropower projects were destroyed, and authorities issued alerts urging residents in several districts to keep away from the Bhotekoshi, Trishuli and Narayani rivers.

“We have asked both India and China to help us with the rescue efforts,” government spokesperson Sasmit Pokharel said.

Rasuwa district was worst hit, echoing similar flash floods in August last year when an overflowing glacial lake in neighbouring Tibet killed nine people and damaged a key cross-border bridge.

Climate experts at the International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development said an ice-rock avalanche on the Nepal side blocked the Lhende Khola, a Bhotekoshi tributary, before releasing a sudden surge downstream, underscoring growing risks in the rapidly warming Himalayas.

images.caption: Damaged houses stand precariously near the swollen, debris-choked banks of the Trishuli river after flash floods in Nepal's Nuwakot district. [Niranjan Shrestha/AP Photo]

A massive flood swept through Nepal's northern Rasuwa district on Wednesday, damaging roads and power infrastructure as authorities scrambled to assess the scale of destruction. [Niranjan Shrestha/AP Photo]
The Nepal army said it had deployed helicopters and disaster responders to the affected area. [Prabin Ranabhat.AFP]
People take photographs and videos of the swollen, debris-choked banks of the Trishuli river after flash floods in Nepal's Nuwakot district. [Niranjan Shrestha/AP Photo]
The Nepal Electricity Authority said about 430 megawatts of production capacity, including from hydropower and solar facilities, has been damaged. [Prakash Mathema/AFP]
Prime Minister Balendra Shah convened an emergency meeting of the National Disaster Risk Reduction and Management Authority to assess the situation. [Niranjan Shrestha/AP Photo]
Monsoon rains from June to September regularly trigger deadly floods and landslides across South Asia. [Prabin Ranabhat/AFP]
A resident sits on the balcony of his house surrounded by floodwaters and debris after flash floods caused the Trishuli river to swell in Nepal's Nuwakot district. [Niranjan Shrestha/AP Photo]
Scientists say climate change is increasing the frequency and intensity of extreme weather events in the region. [Prakash Mathema/AFP]

articles.title: Prince Harry and Meghan arrive back in UK, six years after leaving royal life behind
articles.summary: The Duke and Duchess of Sussex arrived back in the United Kingdom on Wednesday, multiple media outlets reported, six years after they left the country on stepping back from royal life.
articles.body: The Duke and Duchess of Sussex arrived back in the United Kingdom on Wednesday, multiple media outlets reported, six years after they left the country on stepping back from royal life. The BBC, the country’s public broadcaster, earlier reported that Prince Harry and Meghan – along with their two children, Prince Archie and Princess Lilibet – were understood to have flown privately into Britain from California. The Telegraph newspaper reported the family landed around lunchtime on Wednesday at Birmingham Airport. CNN has reached out to the office of the Duke and Duchess of Sussex. The Sussexes’ return to the UK after living in the United States for the past six years was revealed last week. Archie, 7, and Lilibet, 5, are already enrolled in British schools for the coming term, which is due to start in September. Harry and Meghan are returning to the UK as private citizens and will not be resuming any official duties on behalf of King Charles III. The couple left the UK for North America in 2020 after stepping back from royal life, and the years since have seen a public falling out with the wider royal family. Harry and Meghan had cited tabloid intrusion, racism in British institutions, online abuse and complex family dynamics as among the reasons behind their departure. Harry has made several trips back to the UK, including for the funeral of his grandmother Queen Elizabeth II in 2022 and the coronation of his father King Charles III the following year. Security sticking point The family were most recently back in Britain over the summer when they visited King Charles and Queen Camilla at Highgrove, the monarch’s private country residence in Gloucestershire, England. It was the first time the 77-year-old monarch had been reunited with his grandchildren in four years. The Sussexes also spent time with Harry’s mother’s side of the family at Althorp House, the Spencer estate in Northamptonshire. King Charles was only informed of the family’s move earlier this month. Prince William and Catherine, Princess of Wales were also told of the Sussexes’ plans. When asked by CNN last week why they were moving back, a source close to the couple would only remark on how much they enjoyed their visit as a family to the UK last month. Any time Prince Harry has previously returned to the UK, one sticking point has been his family’s close police protection. He has fought a yearslong legal battle against the UK government as his taxpayer-funded security was downgraded by its Royal and VIP Executive Committee (RAVEC) after he and Meghan ceased official work on behalf of the monarch. Since then, it has been determined on a case-by-case basis. Last year, he lost a challenge against the Home Office in the UK Court of Appeal on the decision. At the time, the duke said he couldn’t “see a world in which I would bring my wife and children back to the UK at this point.” It’s unclear if the security arrangements had changed in recent weeks or who would pay for any required security once back in Britain. At the end of June, he was still waiting on a review by RAVEC’s Risk Management Board. A UK government spokesperson has previously described its protective security system as “rigorous and proportionate.” Britain's Prince Harry and his wife Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, are among the most famous couples in the world.Harry, the second son of King Charles III and the late Princess Diana, was introduced to Meghan, an American actress, by mutual friends in 2016. They were married in 2018 in a ceremony watched by millions of people around the world.The two had their first child, Archie, in 2019. They had their second, Lilibet, in 2021.In January 2020, the couple announced that they would be stepping back from their roles as senior members of the British royal family, with a plan to work toward becoming "financially independent."They have lived in the United States for the past few years, but they are planning to move back to Britain, CNN understands. Harry and Meghan are said to be planning to relocate later this month to a private residence outside London, and they reportedly have enrolled their children in British schools for the coming term, according to UK newspaper The Telegraph. Separately in July, Harry and six other high-profile figures lost their privacy case against a British tabloid publisher in the UK High Court. Last week, a judge ruled that the group – which also includes Elton John and his husband David Furnish, must make an initial payment of £9.5 million ($13 million) to Associated Newspapers Limited. However, the group face paying up to a reported £34.5 million ($46.9 million) in total legal costs. Harry and Meghan are settling back in the UK for an extended period of time, according to British media, and will live in a private property outside of London. The pair have not yet spoken publicly about their plans. The duke will likely have charity engagements in the weeks ahead, such as the annual ceremony run by WellChild, a charity that cares for seriously ill children and young people in the UK. Preparations are also underway for his Invictus Games, which will be hosted in Birmingham next year. Meanwhile, Meghan’s latest posts on Instagram suggest she will continue to grow her As Ever lifestyle business.

articles.title: GTA 6 leaks: Rockstar issues statement over online clips
articles.summary: The game developer says the unauthorised footage has caused "heartbreak" for those working on the title.
articles.body:
Grand Theft Auto 6 maker Rockstar Games has issued a statement addressing a series of leaked videos showing the upcoming blockbuster video game.

Clips appearing to show gameplay and cinematics from the title began appearing online last week, but the developer did not acknowledge them straight away.

In a statement, the company said the leaks had been "heartbreaking" for the team working on the sequel, and that they were "not how we intended for you to see the game after all this time".

The company apologised for the delays in releasing official updates on the highly anticipated title, but vowed to "exceed" fans' expectations in a special preview airing on Netflix this week.

When leaks first began to surface, there was some doubt as to whether they were genuine.

But as the days went on, evidence mounted to suggest they were legitimate.

Copies of clips were quickly taken down from social media sites via copyright strikes, where the owner of a work can request its removal.

And, on Friday, Rockstar's parent company Take Two Interactive launched legal proceedings regarding the leaks in a New York court.

Rockstar acknowledged players had been waiting for it to address the leaked footage, and said it was "unfortunate the intended game experience may now be impacted by some spoilers".

It also thanked fans who sent messages of support over the past week, adding: "Your words have meant more to the team than you can imagine."

The group behind the leaks claims to be acting in the interests of players, accusing Rockstar of engaging in anti-consumer practices such as its decision not to release a disc version of GTA 6 at launch .

Not everyone is convinced, as each release of new material has invited viewers to send cryptocurrency "donations" to the user uploading them.

GTA 6, due to be released on PlayStation 5 and Xbox consoles in November, is still expected to be the biggest video game launch of the decade.

The previous game in the series, GTA 5, also broke records when it came out in 2013 and has sold more than 200 million copies since.

Two official trailers for the sixth game have almost 500 million combined views on YouTube, and the Netflix "extended look" on Thursday is being marketed as an event by the streaming service.

Next month the company is due to appear at an employment tribunal in Scotland to defend itself against claims it illegally sacked a group of ex-employees for trying to form a union .

It strongly denies the accusations, and says the workers were fired on the grounds of gross misconduct.

articles.title: 3 Secret Service officials under internal investigation for potential misconduct
articles.summary: Three U.S. Secret Service officials placed on leave amid a misconduct probe as the agency confirms awareness of an Iranian threat against Barron Trump.
articles.body: Three U.S. Secret Service officials were placed on administrative leave on Tuesday pending an internal investigation into potential misconduct. The agency's Office of Professional Responsibility was just beginning its review on Tuesday and did not offer details about what the three officials were being investigated for. The Secret Service public information office noted that the three officials were not working in law enforcement roles at the agency. SECRET SERVICE AGENT ON JD VANCE'S DETAIL INVESTIGATED FOR ALLEGEDLY LEAKING OPERATIONAL SECURITY INFO The Secret Service has faced increased scrutiny under President Donald Trump's administration in the wake of three separate assassination attempts against him. The first attempt, in Butler, Pennsylvania, launched a series of congressional hearings with leaders at the Secret Service. TWO YEARS AFTER BUTLER, THREATS AGAINST TRUMP KEEP ASSASSINATION ATTEMPT IN SHARP FOCUS More recently, the Secret Service said on Tuesday that it was aware of a threat from Iran against the president's youngest son, Barron Trump. "The U.S. Secret Service is aware of the video and investigates anything that can be perceived as a threat toward our protectees," Nate Herring, a Secret Service spokesperson, told Fox News Digital. TRUMP HAS BECOME AMERICA'S MOST TARGETED LEADER, FACING THREATS EVERY FEW MONTHS "Out of concern for operational security, we do not discuss matters of protective intelligence," Herring added. The video depicts locations associated with the younger Trump's whereabouts. It ends with a suggested $10 million reward for his location. TRUMP WARNS US WOULD 'DECIMATE AND DESTROY' IRAN OVER ASSASSINATION ATTEMPT Iranian state media has aired content on multiple occasions threatening Trump and his family following the assassination of Iran's Ayatollah Ali Khamenei, which came at the start of the war between the United States and Iran, as well as the U.S. airstrike that killed Iranian General Qasem Soleimani in 2020. "I don't think it's any secret, it's been in the media, that Iran has publicly said they want to kill President Trump," Deputy Director of the U.S. Secret Service Matt Quinn told reporters at an event last month. TRUMP SAYS HE LEFT INSTRUCTIONS TO 'BOMB' IRAN 'AT LEVELS' NEVER SEEN IF HE IS ASSASSINATED The video came amid threats from the Trump administration to nations that fail to sever their economic ties with Tehran and an ongoing naval blockade of the Strait of Hormuz. articles.title: At least 14 newborns killed in Pakistan nursery hospital fire
articles.summary: Video shows grieving families at Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences after a nursery fire killed 14 infants when an AC unit compressor exploded.
articles.body: At least 14 babies at the Pakistan Institute of Medical Sciences died in a nursery fire Wednesday, while one infant was rescued, according to hospital officials. The blaze at the major government hospital in the capital Islamabad broke out at about 6:45 a.m. after an air conditioning unit compressor exploded, hospital and rescue officials said. The fire was contained to the nursery in the hospital's gynecology ward and did not affect any other hospital wards. "One baby was rescued by a doctor," hospital spokesperson Dr. Aneeza Jalil said, adding that six of the deceased infants' bodies had been given over to families, while the remaining bodies would be given over soon. NYC 5-ALARM FIRE INJURES AT LEAST 17 FIREFIGHTERS, OTHERS AS BLAZE DAMAGES MULTIPLE APARTMENT BUILDINGS Video showed grieving families distraught with sorrow as investigators examined blasted out windows and authorities worked to secure the scene. "I don’t know what to say or whom to blame," a woman The Associated Press (AP) identified as Mrs. Mohammad Sami said. "I have lost my child," she told the outlet, just three days after she reportedly gave birth. TRUMP’S FAVORITE FIELD MARSHAL: WHO IS PAKISTAN’S POWERFUL ARMY CHIEF ASIM MUNIR WITH DEEP INTEL TIES The incident prompted Pakistani Prime Minister Shehbaz Sharif to remove Health Secretary Aslam Ghauri, the country's highest civil servant, from office. Sharif ordered an immediate investigation. "A tragedy involving children is an irreparable loss," he said. Shortly after the incident, Sharif convened a high-level meeting in which he expressed anger at officials for the incident and removed Ghauri. Pakistani President Asif Ali Zardari also weighed in, offering condolences to the families and saying the deaths amounted to a "heartbreaking and an irreparable loss." articles.title: Montana man who killed 4 children, 4 other family members at Sunday dinner was asked to move out: relative
articles.summary: Charlotte Ghekiere, 12, called 911 during a shooting near Billings, Montana, that left eight family members and the suspect dead, according to a report.
articles.body: A Montana man who killed eight of his relatives, including four children, during a Sunday dinner at a home in Montana had been asked by his parents weeks earlier to move out of the property, according to a family member. Brad Ireland told The Associated Press that his former wife and two children were among those killed by Alan Smith, 44, in a homicide that the Billings Police Department called an "unimaginable tragedy." Investigators said Smith died after suffering a self-inflicted gunshot wound. The victims were identified by the AP as Ireland’s ex-wife, Megan Ghekiere, and their two children, Owen Ireland, 13, and Chloe Ireland, 7. Also killed were Ghekiere’s two stepchildren with her current husband: Landon Ghekiere, 15, and Charlotte Ghekiere, 12, as well as Smith’s parents, Dana and Barb, and his grandmother Evelyn. "The one thing we do know is that Charlotte was the hero," Jennifer Mercer, a neighbor and family friend who set up an online fundraiser to help cover funeral costs and other expenses, said to the news agency. "Charlotte called 911 and she tried to save her family. And that’s something the family does want out there." MICHIGAN DAD SHOT WIFE, SIX KIDS THEN SET FAMILY HOME ABLAZE IN MURDER-SUICIDE, SHERIFF SAYS The Billings Police Department said it responded to a 911 call of an active shooting at 6:01 p.m. Sunday and heard shots fired from the back of the house. Minutes later, the property was fully engulfed in flames. Firefighters ultimately fought the blaze until around 1 a.m. Monday, according to Billings Fire Department Chief Matt Hoppel. The home is in a subdivision outside of city limits that’s not required to have fire hydrants. "Due to the condition and structural integrity of the residence, recovery and investigative efforts must be conducted carefully and methodically," the Billings Police Department said Tuesday, adding that, "we extend our sincere and heartfelt condolences to the families and loved ones affected by this unimaginable tragedy." Mercer described the family as "very loving and close," and said the children all got along and that their parents remained amicable even after divorcing. The Smith family was originally from the Seattle area. Ireland said that after he and Megan Ghekiere divorced six years ago, she moved to Montana with their children and met the man who would become her second husband, Adam Ghekiere, who was working and not at the home when the shooting occurred. She and Alan’s parents, Dana and Barb Smith, soon followed, buying a house in Billings near their daughter’s home. Evelyn Smith, their grandmother, lived in a nearby retirement community, Ireland said. Alan Smith, who also moved in with his parents in Montana, was described by Ireland as a "hermit" who spent most of his days in his room on his computer. "No one knew what he did in there 24/7," he said. DISPATCH AUDIO RELEASED IN MICHIGAN FAMILY MURDER-SUICIDE AS TROUBLED FAMILY'S SECRETS EMERGE Smith’s parents had asked Alan to move out weeks ago after he stayed with them for years, Ireland told the AP. Alan Smith had attended Eastern Washington University but had been unable to find or hold a job, the AP reported. Ireland told the news agency that to his knowledge, Alan Smith had never been violent, though he could be verbally abusive. Adam Ghekiere, who works at the airport in Billings, told the AP that he heard over a dispatch radio about an active shooting. After calling each member of his family, he raced across town to the Smith home. When he got there, the house was ablaze, and two hours later, he learned his wife and children had been killed. His children weren't supposed to be there because family dinner was usually on Friday, he said. "I don’t think he expected my kids to be there," Ghekiere said, referring to his brother-in-law. "Monster isn’t even enough to describe what he did." A GoFundMe page said Adam Ghekiere’s 15-year-old son Landon, who was set to enter his sophomore year of high school, was "looking forward to getting his driver’s license this week and was a patient, protective, and loving big brother." CLICK HERE TO DOWNLOAD THE FOX NEWS APP "Charlotte was 12 and preparing to begin seventh grade. Funny, precocious, and adorable -- with just the right amount of stubborn -- Charlotte had an angelic smile and loved posing for pictures," it added. The Associated Press contributed to this report.

articles.title: Americans reported among hundreds missing in Nepal floods, tourism board says
articles.summary: At least three American tourists were reported among a "preliminary" toll.
articles.body:
At least three American tourists were reported among a "preliminary" toll of 384 missing people following serious flash flooding in Nepal, according to a statement posted to X by the Nepal Tourism Board.

The flooding occurred in the northern Rasuwa district, along the border with Tibet, at around 8:30 a.m. local time on Wednesday, authorities said.

The preliminary toll of the missing included 291 foreign nationals and 93 Nepali nationals, the Tourism Board said in its statement.

The three Americans were listed as traveling with a Nepali company called Fishtail Tours and Travel. The agency confirmed to ABC News that three American nationals are among the missing tourists traveling with them.

Efforts to locate and rescue the missing tourists is ongoing, the company said, without providing any further information on their possible whereabouts or wellbeing.

The Nepal Tourism Board said that local tourism and law enforcement authorities were "working to verify the whereabouts and safety status of tourists and travelers who were in or traveling through the affected areas."

The U.S. Embassy in Kathmandu said in posts to X that it was "deeply saddened by the tragic loss of life and devastation" caused by the flooding. "We are closely tracking developments and remain in close contact with Nepali authorities," the embassy said.

The mission also urged Americans to avoid the affected areas and said it was working "to account for U.S. citizens who may have been affected."

Also among the foreign nationals listed as missing in the Tourism Board's preliminary count were Indian, Malaysian, British, South African, Dutch and Australian tourists.

Rescue operations for flood-affected people were ongoing via air transport as of Wednesday, the Nepali Army said in a post to X on Wednesday. The army urged people to adopt high vigilance and stay in safe places.

The flood reportedly inflicted casualties on the Chinese side of the border, at the Gyirong border crossing, according to the Chinese state-run Xinhua News Agency.

President Xi Jinping, the agency reported, ordered search and rescue efforts for those reported missing.

This is a developing story. Please check back for updates.

ABC News' Somayeh Malekian and Charlotte Gardiner contributed to this report.

articles.title: Russia’s baiting and switching Latin Americans to fight its war
articles.summary: They were promised the moon and the stars but found only hell in a foreign land.
articles.body:
Russia seems to be losing the war in Ukraine , both morally and militarily. It was not a quick special operation. It has been a long and costly invasion, in which the Russians have had to seek out mercenaries in foreign countries, including Latin America.

In Mexico , Russia has recruited soldiers through social media platforms such as Facebook. Recruits are offered a $3,000 payment, accommodations, meals and a $28,000 bonus. Mexican authorities have confirmed 14 successful recruitments, although there could be many more.

But all that glitters is not gold. Job offers aimed at attracting potential recruits targeted construction and private security sectors. But upon arrival in Moscow , the plans changed: Their passports were confiscated. They were issued uniforms and sent to the front lines. The promised benefits and wages never materialized.

According to one estimate, since 2024, approximately 1,200 Peruvian citizens have enlisted in the Russian army. The vast majority received offers for jobs in kitchen services, security and transport. The package included a $2,500 monthly salary, accommodation and a bonus ranging from $20,000 to $50,000 .

Colombia has also been targeted by Russian recruitment efforts. After years from guerrilla warfare, terrorism and paramilitary violence, the nation has now a large population of impoverished, unemployed former combatants. They were the perfect target for Russian promises of a better life.

Offers circulating on social media and through word-of-mouth promised a monthly salary of $3,500, a $35,000 bonus and Russian citizenship. None of these promises are ever kept. As always, the Russian government denied any knowledge of these illicit operations, which were being repeated time and again.

Cases have also been reported in El Salvador , involving individuals who traveled to Russia seeking work, a good salary and other lucrative employment incentives. They received none of this; instead, they were sent to the front lines in Ukraine.

In Bolivia , Russia recruited impoverished individuals with similar offers and bonuses ranging from $16,000 to $20,000. Nearly 20 cases have been reported in Santa Cruz. The jobs targeted masons, plumbers, cooks and security guards. They were promised the moon and the stars but found only hell in a foreign land.

Russia has been using Cuban mercenaries since 2023 . The island’s soldiers are familiar with the weapons. They are both trained and paid cheaply, reducing Putin’s political cost to zero. No one in Moscow will complain about the deaths of foreign soldiers.

In 2025, Cuba took things to a new level. The number of Cuban mercenaries sent to Ukraine is on the rise, reaching 20,000 soldiers . The trend shows that Cuba could even surpass the number of troops coming from North Korea or failed African nations.

The young Cubans enlisted as Russian troops believed in promises of money and well-being for their families on the island. Instead, they have only found death, deception and dishonor. The Russian regime takes advantage of the need and desperation being experienced in Cuba and other countries. The offer includes $2,000 a month, Russian citizenship and 15 days of vacation every six months. It is an attractive promise that Putin has only half-fulfilled, generating desertions and discontent.

Russia is not winning the war, no matter how many churches, schools or civilian apartment buildings it bombs. In fact, it the day it invaded a sovereign country and decided to profit from poverty, recruiting soldiers through lies and false promises.

Russia’s strategy is illegal and criminal, yet unsurprising. Nevertheless, Latin American governments, with the support of the U.S., should join efforts to counter these deceptive Russian maneuvers and ensure that the Americas remain a free, prosperous and secure region for all.

Arturo McFields is an exiled journalist, former Nicaraguan ambassador to the Organization of American States, and a former member of the Norwegian Peace Corps. He is an alumnus of the National Defense University’s Security and Defense Seminar and the Harvard Leadership course.

articles.title: Prince Harry, Meghan and children arrive in UK after 6 years
articles.summary: UK News: Prince Harry and Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, have returned to the UK with their children, Archie and Lilibet, marking their first visit since stepping back from royal duties. The family is expected to live as private citizens in the Cotswolds while their children prepare for school. This visit raises questions about Harry's security arrangements following a recent legal dispute.
articles.body: Prince Harry and Meghan, Duchess of Sussex, have returned to the UK after 6 years with their children, Archie and Lilibet, The Telegraph reported.The Sussexes landed at Birmingham Airport around lunchtime on Wednesday after travelling privately from California. The family is expected to base themselves at a home in the Cotswolds, where they will live as private citizens rather than working members of the Royal Family.Their children have been enrolled in school in the UK, with the new academic term due to begin next week.A source told The Telegraph that âHow long will they stay? articles.title: Ice avalanche, glacial lake or earthquake? What triggered Nepalâs deadly floods
articles.summary: South Asia News: Floods battered Nepal on Wednesday after a sudden surge in the Bhote Koshi River swept through the Rasuwa district near the China border, killing over.
articles.body: Floods battered Nepal on Wednesday after a sudden surge in the Bhote Koshi River swept through the Rasuwa district near the China border, killing over 30 people and leaving hundreds of people, including foreign nationals, reported missing.The cause of the devastating flash flood is now being investigated, with an initial assessment suggesting that an ice avalanche may have blocked the Lhende River, causing water to build up before suddenly bursting downstream.According to The Kathmandu Post, Rijan Bhakta Kayastha, a professor at Kathmandu University and climate researcher, said the preliminary assessment was based on discussions with scientists in Nepal and China. He said an ice avalanche from the Nepal side appeared to have fallen into the Lhende River and blocked its flow.âThere is information that an ice avalanche from the Nepal side blocked the Lhende river,â Kayastha said, according to The Kathmandu Post. âAn earthquake also occurred on the Tibetan side around the same time.âThe US Geological Survey recorded a magnitude 4.4 earthquake in Tibetan territory at 8:37am, around 47 kilometres north of Gosainkunda. However, it remains unclear whether the earthquake played any role in triggering the flood.Scientists are also investigating whether a glacial lake outburst contributed to the disaster. Kayastha said it could take several days to establish whether a glacial lake had burst, noting that the region contains several large glacial lakes.A similar disaster struck the area on July 8, 2025, when a sudden flood in the Lhende River was attributed to a glacial lake outburst. Satellite imagery at the time indicated that a glacial lake had burst near the Nepal-China border.The latest flooding struck the Bhote Koshi River at around 8:30am, damaging settlements and infrastructure and sweeping away people and vehicles.Nepal Tourism Board said 384 travellers, including 291 foreign nationals and 93 Nepali nationals, had been reported missing based on preliminary information. Around 105 Indians were among those reported missing, while 37 non-resident Indians were reported missing from the Himalayan Glacier area.Rescue operations continued through Wednesday, with authorities urging residents along the Trishuli River to move to safer areas as floodwaters moved downstream.India has also offered assistance. Prime Minister Narendra Modi spoke to Nepal Prime Minister Balendra Shah and said India was ready to provide âall possible humanitarian assistanceâ, adding that teams from both countries were coordinating rescue and relief efforts.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Nepal floods: Terrifying videos show homes, buildings and bridges swallowed by raging waters
articles.summary: South Asia News: Nepal: A sudden flood in the Bhotekoshi River battered Nepalâs Rasuwa district on Wednesday morning, sweeping through settlements and causing widespre.
articles.body: Nepal: A sudden flood in the Bhotekoshi River battered Nepalâs Rasuwa district on Wednesday morning, sweeping through settlements and causing widespread destruction. Houses, bridges and other structures were damaged as muddy floodwaters surged through the area, with several people reported missing.Dramatic visuals circulating on social media show the scale of the flooding, with torrents of brown water rushing through communities and engulfing buildings and bridges. In some videos, structures appear to be swept away within seconds as the powerful current tears through the area. The visuals also show people struggling to move to safer ground as the floodwaters rapidly rise.The sudden surge has left large parts of the affected area severely damaged. Roads and bridges have been inundated, while homes and public infrastructure have been damaged by the force of the water. Several people are missing, although authorities have yet to release a confirmed toll of deaths, injuries or the full extent of property damage, according to The Kathmandu Post.Rasuwa Chief District Officer Narendra Pariyar said the cause of the sudden flood remained unclear. He said the weather in the area had been sunny and authorities were investigating whether the surge could have been linked to a glacier burst or another event upstream.Authorities have issued high alerts and urged residents living along the Trishuli River basin to move to safer locations. People in areas including Nuwakot, Dhading, Chitwan and Gorkha, particularly those living close to riverbanks, have been advised to evacuate as water levels in the Bhotekoshi River rise.According to a list provided by Nepalâs National Tourism Board, more than 100 Indians and 37 non-resident Indians (NRIs) are reported missing following the disaster.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: In 1976, Michigan created a conservation fund from oil, gas and mineral revenues; 50 years later it has awarded nearly $1.4 billion and is putting $6.5 million toward almost 22,650 Keweenaw acres
articles.summary: US News: Michigan has awarded nearly $1.4 billion for land protection and recreation projects across the state. The Michigan Natural Resources Trust Fund that .
articles.body: Michigan has awarded nearly $1.4 billion for land protection and recreation projects across the state. The Michigan Natural Resources Trust Fund that was created in 1976, is also marking 50 years of a conservation fund that has used earnings from the stateâs oil, gas and mineral revenues to support public land and outdoor recreation.According to Michigan state government official site, the latest funding comes through Michiganâs fiscal year 2027 budget. It includes $45 million in Trust Fund grants for 75 land acquisition and park development projects. The grants are expected to combine with nearly $64 million in local and matching funds, creating a total investment of $108.9 million in public land and outdoor recreation.One of the biggest allocations is for the Keweenaw Peninsula. The Michigan Department of Natural Resources will receive $6.5 million to acquire nearly 22,650 acres. The land acquisition will consolidate state-managed land for recreation and natural resource protection.The funding also includes $1.5 million for the DNR to acquire 460 acres next to Porcupine Mountains Wilderness State Park. The land includes wooded hills, trout streams and wildlife habitats. Another $5 million will help the DNR acquire more than 1,400 acres of forestland, including all of Turtle Lake and nearly two miles of the Turtle Creek corridor, to protect habitat and water quality in the Au Sable River watershed.Turning resource revenues into conservationThe Michigan Natural Resources Trust Fund is a restricted fund established to support the public acquisition of land for resource protection and outdoor recreation. s The fund is financed through interest and earnings from revenues generated by state-owned oil, gas and mineral leases.The Trust Fund is administered by the Michigan Department of Natural Resources and was placed in Michiganâs Constitution for permanent protection. Over five decades, it has supported land purchases, land rights and improvements to outdoor recreation facilities across the state.According to DNR Director Scott Bowen,âSince its inception, the Trust Fund has awarded crucial grant dollars to local governments and state agencies for creative projects and acquisitions that greatly benefit residents and local economies in every county of the state.â75 projects receive fundingThe fiscal year 2027 budget supports projects across Michigan, covering both land acquisitions and improvements to existing parks and trails.Among the acquisition projects, East Bay Township will receive $4.8 million to acquire an easement on 333 acres known as the Ridge Nature Preserve. The project will protect public access and future trail connections to the Traverse Area Recreation and Transportation trail system.Saugatuck Township will receive $2.5 million to acquire 119 acres along the Kalamazoo River. The property includes more than 2,200 feet of river frontage and is planned as a destination park and nature preserve.The DNR will also receive $1.6 million to acquire 354 acres of oak-pine barrens habitat in Newaygo County. The acquisition will connect the east and west units of the Muskegon State Game Area.Other acquisitions include former railway land for the North Country National Scenic Trail and Michiganâs Iron Belle Trail, waterfront land along Pettyâs Bayou and additional land along the Grand River and Black River.The development grants will fund a wide range of improvements. Projects include accessible trails, playgrounds, boat launches, boardwalks, restrooms, parking areas, trailheads and waterfront facilities.The city of Grayling, for example, will receive $400,000 to build a 1.8-mile shared-use pathway along M-72. In Detroit, $400,000 will support an inclusive playground at Clemente Park, along with parking, a multi-sport court and landscaping.Other projects include a new accessible path through Bliss Park in Saginaw, improvements to Rosy Mound Natural Area in Ottawa County and a three-mile extension of the Blue Star Trail in Saugatuck Township.Fund has also shaped Detroit RiverfrontThe Trust Fundâs impact can also be seen along Detroitâs riverfront. In June, the Michigan DNR highlighted projects supported through decades of state and local partnerships.The Detroit Riverfront attracts about 3 million people each year and has received more than $45 million in Trust Fund-supported community investment through different projects.At Ralph C. Wilson, Jr. Centennial Park, $5.7 million in Trust Fund support helped create connections to the riverfront, including the West Riverfront Connector. The 22-acre park has play areas, a water garden, a sport house and landscaped paths.The William G. Milliken State Park and Harbor has received $26.25 million in Trust Fund funding. Projects there include a 1,500-foot pedestrian trail, the final connection of the Detroit East Riverwalk through the park and land and easement acquisitions along the Detroit River.Trust Fund support also helped acquire 48,000 square feet of space in the historic Globe Building for the DNR Outdoor Adventure Center. Another $3.4 million supported work linked to the Belle Isle Iron Belle Trail and Ralph C. Wilson, Jr. Trail.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. Download the TOI app.

articles.title: Anne Donaghy: Ex-council chief convicted of two charges over email deletion
articles.summary: Her co-accused Aaron McClelland was also cleared of trying to have an email deleted.
articles.body:
A former chief executive of Mid and East Antrim Council has been convicted of two charges connected to deleting or attempting to delete an email to prevent disclosure under the Freedom of Information Act.

Anne Donaghy, 56, of Clonmore Road, Dungannon, has been fined £1,500. She was cleared of a third charge of trying to have an email deleted.

Her co-accused Aaron McClelland, of Clonmakate Road in Portadown, was also cleared of one charge of trying to have an email deleted.

The charges Donaghy was convicted of relate to an email she sent to the private email address of then-Democratic Unionist Party (DUP) leader Arlene Foster.

Donaghy was cleared of a charge related to an email sent to DUP councillor Greg McKeen.

District Judge Alana McSorley told the court Donaghy had been under mounting political pressure at the time she told her PA to delete the email to Foster.

She said a perception that Donaghy had been too close to the DUP "formed the basis" of Donaghy's decision to delete the email.

The judge said the "irrefutable conclusion" was that Donaghy had intended to prevent disclosure of information.

articles.title: Who was Andreethegirl? TikToker Andree Greig Baudoin dies at 39 after cancer battle
articles.summary: US Streamers News: TikToker Andree Greig Baudoin, better known online as Andreethegirl, has died at the age of 39 after a long battle with metastatic cancer. Baudoin use.
articles.body: TikToker Andree Greig Baudoin, better known online as Andreethegirl, has died at the age of 39 after a long battle with metastatic cancer. Baudoin used TikTok to openly share her life, treatment, fears, and hopes with her followers. She died on August 22 at Calcutta House by Hospice of Acadiana in Lafayette, Louisiana. After her death, a video she had recorded before entering hospice was posted on her account. In the emotional message, she said goodbye to her TikTok family and thanked them for supporting her journey.Who was Andreethegirl and why did she turn TikTok into a cancer diary?Andree Greig Baudoin became known on TikTok as Andreethegirl, where she shared personal videos about her life and cancer battle. She first created the account for her children. She wanted them to have videos they could watch later and remember her.Over time, however, TikTok became much more important to Baudoin. She described the account as her âdiaryâ and a place where she could share her feelings. Her followers watched as she went through different treatments and tried different ways to fight her cancer.Baudoin said she tried many options during her battle. She traveled to Mexico for treatment and also tried different therapies, diets, and medicines. Later, she hoped to join a clinical trial. However, she said she was told she could not take part.Her health then became much worse. Baudoin eventually learned that the cancer had progressed so much that there were no more treatments that could help her.Andreethegirlâs final TikTok message thanked her followersBefore her death, Baudoin recorded a final message for her followers. The video was later posted to her TikTok account so her community could hear her goodbye.âIf youâre seeing this video, it just means that my time has come and Iâve crossed over,â she said at the beginning of the message.Baudoin explained that she was not afraid of dying, but she was heartbroken about leaving her husband and children. She said she would never get to see her children get married, meet her grandchildren, or grow old with her husband.She also explained that she wanted to stay at home for as long as possible. But when the time came, she moved to Calcutta House. She did not want to die in her family home because she wanted the house to remain a place filled with life and memories.In her final words, Baudoin thanked her followers for loving, praying for, and supporting her. She also shared one final wish: that people should not take their health or everyday life for granted.âEnjoy the day in front of you,â she told her followers.Baudoinâs final video left a lasting message for the TikTok community that had followed her journey. Through her posts, she turned a difficult personal battle into a story that allowed others to learn from her experiences and remember her after her death.Catch the latest World News and Live updates. articles.title: Acceptance ran through Dolly Parton's lyrics, Newcastle PhD writer says
articles.summary: Fans from the North East and Cumbria pay tribute, including James Barker who wrote his thesis on her.
articles.body:
A man who spent five years studying Dolly Parton's lyrics for his PhD says acceptance ran through her music.

James Barker, 34, wrote his thesis at Newcastle University exploring LGBTQ+ inclusion in the country music industry, and said Parton created a "space where a lot of LGBTQIA+ listeners can hear themselves".

Tributes have been pouring in for the country music icon who died on Tuesday aged 80, including from former BBC Radio Tees presenter Stan Laundon who said she was a "bundle of fun".

Cumbrian superfan Joe Skelly, who ran her official UK fan club for many years, said she was "very, very remarkable" and planned to create a music room in his house for his hundreds of pieces of memorabilia.

Studying over the Covid-19 pandemic, Barker started each day listening to a new Dolly Parton song.

The title of his PhD took a line from her song Family: "Some are are preachers, some are gay, some are addicts, drunks and strays and not a one is turned away."

He said: "You have the explicit message of acceptance in a country song in the early 1990s.

"There's a caricature of Dolly, but the kindness she has, it's really quite genuine and deep-rooted when you listen to the songs.

"Country is an identity that's very, kind of, gatekept.

"But she created this space where a lot of LGBTQIA+ listeners can hear themselves."

Skelly, 57, from Seaton near Workington, met Parton on several occasions.

"Her gaze would be on you the whole time while you were making the point or discussing whatever subject you were talking about.

"Royalty could have walked in the room, she wouldn't have taken her gaze and her attention off you until you'd finished."

He is in the process of converting his attic into a music room dedicated to Dolly.

"I have every book ever written, I have every record ever pressed, I have every CD ever made," Skelly said.

"I have about 950 to 1,000 pieces of just physical music memorabilia.

"I'll be able to get everything out and put it in one place where I can just go and reflect."

Stan Laundon previously presented a country music show on BBC Radio Tees and managed to meet and interview Dolly Parton.

"She was a bundle of fun," Laundon said.

"A friend of mine who was with me took a photo with me and Dolly together, and he was so excited the camera was shaking and the photograph was out of focus."

He recalls asking her for an autograph but because she did not have any photos on her, she offered to send it to his address.

"Well, a couple of weeks later I got two ten by eight photographs, one signed to me, one signed to my wife."

articles.title: At least 19 dead and more than 380 tourists missing after flash flooding in Nepal
articles.summary: Monsoon rains from June to September regularly trigger deadly floods and landslides across South Asia.
articles.body:
Over 380 tourists, mostly foreigners, were out of contact in Nepal on Wednesday after a massive flood tore through the border region with Tibet.

"A preliminary agency-wise record received from tourism and travel companies has identified 384 travellers, including 291 foreign nationals and 93 Nepali nationals, who were reported missing from the affected areas," said Nepal Tourism Board, noting authorities were working to verify the travellers' whereabouts.

"Nineteen bodies have been recovered so far. We are intensely coordinating the rescue and relief efforts. Many in our police force are also out of contact," Nepali police spokesperson Abi Narayan Kafle said.

Videos shared by Nepal police and others on social media showed torrents of muddy water crashing through mountain valleys in the Himalayan district bordering China.

"I witnessed the flood sweep away eight or nine trucks, along with houses and people," Suman Chalise, a 34-year-old teacher, told AFP in Nuwakot district.

"It was absolutely heart-wrenching. I had not witnessed such devastation before."

The police spokesperson said earlier that authorities did not know the extent of the damage but said they had "alerted people who are staying near the riverside to relocate."

The Nepal Army said it had deployed helicopters and disaster response personnel to the affected area.

The Nepal Electricity Authority said about 430 megawatts of production capacity, including from hydropower and solar facilities, has been damaged.

"The disaster has damaged the production, transmission and distribution facilities of the Authority...resulting in disruption of electricity supply," it said.

Sarthak Shrestha, a remote sensing and geo information analyst at the Kathmandu-based International Centre for Integrated Mountain Development (ICIMOD), said a preliminary assessment showed "no anomalies" from China's side of the border.

"We believe a rock-ice avalanche occurred in Nepal, blocking the Lhende river and causing the cascading flood event," he said.

Several highways were also closed, Nepali authorities said.

Chinese state broadcaster CCTV reported on Wednesday that "a mudslide disaster on the Nepalese side resulted in major casualties and missing people at the Gyirong Port" in Tibet.

Footage shared by the broadcaster, showed rushing water carrying tree branches and debris, as well as a flooded road.

State news agency Xinhua said Chinese President Xi Jinping had urged "all-out" rescue operations, but did not provide figures on injuries or deaths.

Xi said that "the most urgent task is doing everything possible to search for and rescue the missing people...quickly treat injured people and minimise casualties to the greatest extent possible," according to CCTV.

Traffic authorities in Tibet's Shigatse said roads in the area were "at risk of mudslides and unsafe for passage" in a post on social media on Wednesday.

In July last year, 17 people went missing after a mudslide near the Gyirong Port, Xinhua reported at the time.

Monsoon rains from June to September regularly trigger deadly floods and landslides across South Asia.

articles.title: Impact of Dolly Parton's Imagination Library praised
articles.summary: The former Reading MP said he believed the town was the second place in the country to get books.
articles.body:
The impact of Dolly Parton's children's literary scheme has been praised by a former MP who helped bring the scheme to his constituency.

Tributes have been poured in for the country singer who died aged 80 . Her Imagination Library has had a presence across the South since it was launched in the UK in 2007.

Martin Salter, who was the MP for Reading West from 1997 until 2010, said he believed his constituency was the second place in the country to receive books.

Just over 3 million children are thought to have benefited from the scheme, which operates in the United States, UK, Australia, Canada and Ireland, with more than 330 million books distributed.

Salter said the aim of the scheme was the put books in homes where "reading was not the norm" and that Parton will be remembered in part for her "generosity and philanthropy".

Her programme was first launched in Sevier County, Tennessee, where the star grew up and was first inspired by her illiterate father.

Salter said it was a good tool in trying to normalise reading in homes where that might not have taken place otherwise.

He said: "In my time in public life in Reading, I've seen some pretty heart wrenching stuff – kids who are scared to bring homework home because their father can't read and doesn't want books in the house. What chance has a kid like that got?"

Children in Hampshire are amongst those who are current recipients of books from the Imagination Library, while other beneficiaries have lived in Blackbird Leys, Rose Hill, Berinsfield and Littlemore in Oxfordshire.

Colin Larkin, the founder and former editor of the Encyclopedia of Popular Music, who is from Poundbury, Dorset, said Parton's legacy as a performer is "remarkable".

He added: "She was the greatest country singer of all time. But beyond that she was an incredible icon. There's no dirt on her; there's no scandal. She had a marriage that lasted 60 years before her husband died last year.

"She had the persona of a dumb blonde – she was the absolute opposite of that. She was such a smart woman. She appealed to everybody - to women, in particular."

Her legacy will "unquestionably" continue, Larkin added.

"It's like The Beatles, an icon like that, that will go on and on."

articles.title: US halts immigrant visa applications for global ‘in-depth’ training course
articles.summary: The Trump administration has paused immigrant visa appointments worldwide to carry out “in-depth training” for consular officers to screen out foreign applicants at risk of taking advantage of U.S. public assistance. The guidance from the State Department comes after a federal judge last week vacated President Trump’s policy suspending visa processing from 75 countries whose…
articles.body:
The Trump administration has paused immigrant visa appointments worldwide to carry out “in-depth training” for consular officers to screen out foreign applicants at risk of taking advantage of U.S. public assistance.

The guidance from the State Department comes after a federal judge last week vacated President Trump’s policy suspending visa processing from 75 countries whose nationals the administration deemed likely to require public assistance.

“A more prosperous American means ensuring that visa applicants are not likely to become a public charge, as defined under U.S. law and regulation, and not likely to become dependent on U.S. public benefits reserved for qualified Americans in need,” a State Department spokesperson told The Hill in an email on Wednesday.

The spokesperson said that a global, in-depth training initiative was launched in early August at all U.S. embassies and consulates worldwide and that “appointments for visa and services will be adjusted.”

“Whenever there are changes to visa interview appointments, embassies and consulates communicate any changes directly to visa applicants,” the spokesperson said.

The pause on visa applications follows Trump’s hardline tack on immigration, where the administration has boasted about revoking more than 175,000 visas from individuals it said had violated the terms by committing criminal offenses, but that largely relied on encounters with law enforcement. The administration announced on Monday it was working to revoke short-term visas from individuals who used them to enter the U.S. and then file asylum claims, with some reports claiming the administration has a goal of canceling 200,000 visas.

The administration has also prioritized revoking visas and permanent residency, or green cards, from people who it deems are a threat to U.S. national security, but advocates say officials are targeting protected free speech like political opinions and pro-Palestinian protests.

But the Trump administration’s policy has received legal pushback. In a ruling on Friday, U.S. District Judge Jeannette Vargas, an appointee of former President Biden, said the Trump administration had exceeded its authority in pausing visa processing for 75 countries , saying a person’s nationality does not indicate they do not have the financial means to support themselves in the U.S.

The judge said that consular officers have the exclusive authority to evaluate visa applicants individually.

images.caption: The State Department in Washington, D.C., is seen on March 30, 2026.

articles.title: Meta agrees to pay up to $16.7bn to settle social media case
articles.summary: The deal has been reached during a California federal court trial over claims brought by 29 states.
articles.body:
Social media giant Meta has reached a settlement with 29 US states to resolve a court case related to child safety on Facebook and Instagram.

The tech company will pay a maximum of $16.68bn (£12.26bn), according to court documents.

The court judgement requires Meta introduce certain rules for teenage users, including daily limits and night-time blocks.

Meta denied wrongdoing in agreeing to settle.

articles.title: Meta settles social media addiction suit for up to $16 billion
articles.summary: Meta Platforms, the owner of Facebook and Instagram has agreed to settle a social media addiction lawsuit for up to $16 billion.
articles.body: Meta Platforms, the owner of Facebook and Instagram, on Wednesday agreed to settle a wide-ranging social media addiction lawsuit with the state of California and a number of other states. A court filing indicates that Meta agreed to pay up to $16.68 billion to bring the case to an end. The filing also says that the company “denies the allegations against it and that it has any liability to the Plaintiffs,” which are a collection of 29 states. As part of the deal, “Meta commits to establishing daily limits and blocks on nighttime use for teenage users” as well as “enhanced age assurance measures to prevent children from accessing the platform, or age restricted content available on the platform,” the court filing also says. The settlement also requires the company to create “additional tools to help parents and guardians to protect their children online.” The announced settlement will require the approval of a judge. The agreement comes one day after Instagram chief Adam Mosseri took the stand in California. In the case, attorneys general from states including California, Colorado, Kentucky and New Jersey accused Meta of harming children with its social media products, which they argued were designed to be addictive. They also accused Meta of violating federal privacy and consumer protection laws. The tech company’s platforms, which include Facebook and Instagram, helped stoke a national mental health crisis among teens and kids, according to the states. Meta, meanwhile, maintained a position that the states were cherry-picking certain features and ignoring the safety tools it has built for young users, including teen accounts, which automatically go private, in addition to other tools like time-limit reminders, parental supervision capabilities and restrictions on who can contact teens and what content they can see. The trial was just one of several Meta has faced with similar claims. In March, a New Mexico jury and judge fined Meta over $900 million after the state’s attorney general argued that it’s platforms created a public nuisance. In California, a state court found that Meta and Google were liable after a young woman said the tech companies, among others, contributed to her deteriorated mental health. Meta did not immediately respond to a request for comment.
